Class PortentaHatCarrier

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.carrier.PortentaHatCarrier
public final class PortentaHatCarrier extends Object
Pin map for the Arduino Portenta Hat Carrier (ASX00049) with a Portenta H7 on it. The carrier's 40-pin header uses the Raspberry Pi physical numbering and carries the H7's SPI bus on pins 19, 21, 23 and 24, so MCU.getSpi() reaches a HAT's SPI device with no extra wiring. Pins here are the Juno names the H7 accepts:
  • Pin 19 MOSI, 21 MISO, 23 SCLK and 24 CE0: the SPI bus, D8, D10, D9 and D7 (MCU.getSpi()).
  • Pin 18, the data/command line of a HAT display: getLcdDataCommand(), Portenta pin PI7, which has no Arduino number and is reached through the H7 core's raw pin index 161.
  • Pin 22, a display's reset: getLcdReset(), D5.
  • Pin 24, the display's chip select: getLcdChipSelect(), D7.
  • Pin 26, a touch controller's chip select: getTouchChipSelect(), D4.

The carrier's microSD slot is not on the header: it is the H7's SDMMC2 bus, which needs no Juno pin name, and getSdCard() is its card.

Create it once, at startup, and pass it to the HAT's driver.

See Also:

  • Method Details

    • getSdCard

      public SdCard getSdCard()
      The card in the carrier's own microSD slot (J7), not the H7's: the slot is on the SDMMC2 bus, so it has no chip select and does not share the header's SPI bus with a HAT display. The same instance every call; its SdCard.begin() mounts the card, and java.io.RandomAccessFile reads files from it.
